question.text: A projectile is given an initial velocity of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi mathvariant="normal">i</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mover accent="true"><mi mathvariant="normal">j</mi><mo>^</mo></mover></mrow></mfenced><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>, where <math> <mrow> <mover accent="true"> <mtext>i</mtext> <mo>^</mo> </mover> </mrow> </math> is along the ground and <math> <mrow> <mover accent="true"> <mtext>j</mtext> <mo>^</mo> </mover> </mrow> </math> is along the vertical upward. If <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>g</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn><mo> </mo><mo>m</mo><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></math>, the equation of its trajectory is :

solution.text:
v → = i ^ + 2 j ^

⇒ x = t    ..... (i)

y = 2 t - 1 2 1 0 t 2    ..... (ii)

From (i) and (ii)
